method.summary: Median of 3 interleaved Rust/React pairs on one shared, busy machine (load 10-21). Ratios matter, absolute numbers do not.
method.workload: Same history, same streamed demo reply (reasoning, then the answer, one word every 18 ms), same 60 s window. Upstream is the published @assistant-ui/react 0.15.33 and @assistant-ui/react-markdown 0.14.25 in headless Chromium.
method.cpu: Whole process tree, every thread and process.
method.memory: Resident memory. React: every Chromium process (RSS; PSS is lower, see each row).
method.source: docs/STATUS.md, section Performance, Against upstream (React); harness in benchmarks/react-baseline

limits: Compared with upstream assistant-ui only. Nothing here says anything about ChatGPT or any other product.
The Rust figures include software rasterisation on the CPU (--bench-render). Chromium's figures include its own raster and compositor work.
The React thread follows upstream's default structure with plain CSS instead of Tailwind and Radix, so it does somewhat less work than upstream's default.
Rust draws at most 60 frames a second, like a display. The shared machine adds noise to every absolute number.
Ratios are rounded down to one decimal, never up. Where the source gives a range, the ratio uses the range end that is less favourable to Rust.

scale.react: The page did not survive in headless Chromium: the browser closed mid-run, and on a second attempt at launch. The harness also could not type a 512 KB prompt into its composer within 30 s.

gpu.title: Real GPU window, Rust only
gpu.conditions: FemtoVG-WGPU, Intel UHD, Wayland. 30 s streaming a ~9 KB reply into a 1000-message thread. Process CPU and peak RSS from /usr/bin/time, interleaved runs. Before and after carrying femtovg fix #366 as a patch.

web.conditions: Headless Chromium 1248 (Playwright 1.64.1), software WebGL (SwiftShader, no GPU), viewport 1000x700, one shared 12-core Linux machine under load; median of 3 fresh runs per row; values rounded to the shown precision. The GPU is emulated on a busy CPU, so frame rates are a floor, not what a real browser GPU gives. The demo model replies one word every 18 ms.
